companyDescription: Rare earth + lithium developer · 92.5% owner of Tanbreez (Greenland, one of the largest known heavy-REE resources globally) + Wolfsberg Lithium (Austria, BMW offtake) + Romania refinery JV with Nuclearelectrica (NATO/EU defense-magnet supply chain) · pending all-share acquisition of European Lithium — court-ordered Scheme Meetings set for Oct 22, 2026 · finalist in Kenya's Mrima Hill rare-earth/niobium government tender
priceNote: Close of $7.65 on Sep 28, 2026 (-2.3%). The Aug 11 report priced this at $6.38; the stock then ran to a $9.33 peak on Sep 21 (+46% cumulative) as a Sep 15 court ruling cleared the path to the Oct 22 EGM and a Sep 16 Tanbreez refinery yield breakthrough landed — then gave back ~18% into month-end profit-taking. Net +20% since the last report. 52-week range now $5.12-$32.15.
sector: Materials / Rare Earth & Critical Minerals Mining
summary: The catalyst that anchored the Aug report — a 'late August' EGM — actually landed as a hard, court-ordered date: European Lithium's Scheme Meetings are now set for Oct 22, 2026 (Scheme Booklet dispatched ~Sep 22, court approval granted Sep 15), with implementation targeted November 2026 and a Nasdaq listing for the combined entity expected ~Nov 6. The deal mechanics also changed materially: the fixed 0.035 exchange ratio became a floating 0.025-0.045 cap/collar band, and EuLi holders will own ~41% of the combined company — real, mechanical dilution independent of the previously-flagged A$36.5-37M EuLi cash shortfall, whose resolution status hasn't resurfaced in recent coverage and is therefore unconfirmed, not verified closed. Unusually, the market broke its own 'sell CRML's good news' pattern this cycle: shares ran +46% from the Aug 11 report price into a Sep 21 peak on the court-clearance + a Sep 16 Tanbreez refinery breakthrough (99% dissolution of eudialyte concentrate into 19 ultra-high-purity REE products, implying $1.8-2.2B in potential annual refinery revenue), before giving back ~18% into Sep 28 on profit-taking. Kenya's Mrima Hill tender remains unresolved — still 1 of 3 finalists, no award date. Survival check clears: cash stood at $102.5M as of Jun 30, 2026 (up from $7.3M a year earlier via 2025 PIPE financings), against negative working capital of ~-$15.4M and positive equity of $368M — no active shelf/ATM identified, so this is a dilution-and-execution story, not a near-term financing-risk one. Thesis intact but re-anchored: the Oct 22 EGM is now the clean, dated binary this report is built around.

catalysts.name: European Lithium Scheme Meetings / EGM Vote — Oct 22, 2026
catalysts.description: Court-ordered general meeting and Scheme Meetings for European Lithium security-holders, in West Leederville, Western Australia. Requires shareholder approval of the scheme resolutions (Scheme Booklet dispatched ~Sep 22, 2026) plus subsequent Australian court confirmation. The exchange ratio is now a floating 0.025-0.045 cap/collar band (vs the original fixed 0.035), and EuLi holders will own ~41% of the combined company post-close. The previously-disclosed ~A$36.5-37M EuLi minimum-cash shortfall has not resurfaced in recent coverage — its resolution is unconfirmed, not verified closed.

catalysts.name: Merger Implementation + Nasdaq Listing (if approved)
catalysts.description: If the Oct 22 vote and subsequent court confirmation succeed, implementation is targeted for November 2026 — ASX delisting of European Lithium ~Oct 27, 2026, Nasdaq listing of the combined entity ~Nov 6, 2026.

catalysts.name: Kenya Mrima Hill Rare Earth/Niobium Tender — Final Round
catalysts.description: The Mrima Earth Limited Consortium, led by Critical Metals, remains one of three finalists in Kenya's government tender for the Mrima Hill rare-earth + niobium project. No award date disclosed as of late Sep 2026.

catalysts.name: Tanbreez Refinery Scale-Up (Romania JV)
catalysts.description: Sep 16, 2026 metallurgical results showed 99% dissolution of eudialyte concentrate into 19 ultra-high-purity rare-earth products, with projected annual refinery revenue of $1.8-2.2B if scaled — an ongoing de-risking process, not a single dated event.

risks: Merger dilution is mechanical and real: European Lithium shareholders will hold ~41% of the combined company, and the exchange ratio is now a floating 0.025-0.045 cap/collar band tied to CRML's own share price below $8.00 — independent of any cash-gap issue

The previously-disclosed ~A$36.5-37M EuLi minimum-cash shortfall against the scheme's A$330M threshold has not resurfaced in recent (Sep 2026) coverage — its resolution status is unconfirmed, not verified closed, ahead of the Oct 22 dual-majority vote
Still pre-revenue; Kenya Mrima Hill remains only a tender finalist (1 of 3) with no award date, and Tanbreez itself is still a pilot-plant/refinery-validation story, not production

Extreme volatility persists: shares ran from $6.38 (Aug 11) to a $9.33 peak (Sep 21) then gave back ~18% into the Sep 28 close on profit-taking — both directions can move fast and can decouple from company-specific news

Negative working capital (~-$15.4M as of Jun 30, 2026) despite a much-improved $102.5M cash position (up from $7.3M a year earlier via 2025 PIPE financings) — the balance sheet is adequate but leans on continued capital-markets access
Shares outstanding grew ~19% over the past year from financing activity; the pending EuLi share issuance adds materially more dilution before the combined story is done

catalystSpot.preRunup: This report period broke CRML's earlier 'sell the news' pattern: the stock rallied continuously from the Aug 11 report price of $6.38 to a Sep 21 peak of $9.33 (+46% cumulative), coinciding with the Sep 15 court ruling clearing the path to the Oct 22 EGM and the Sep 16 Tanbreez refinery yield breakthrough — evidence the market anticipated the court clearance and processing validation rather than only reacting same-day, as it had all year. Since the Sep 21 peak, shares have given back ~18% into the Sep 28 close on profit-taking.
catalystSpot.preRunupTiming: ~5-6 weeks of anticipatory drift this cycle (Aug 11 report to Sep 21 peak) — a change from the prior 'no drift, same-day-only' pattern

postWin.note: Blends two real 2026 events: the Aug 3 sector-wide same-day pop (+16.2%, zero company news) and the Sep 15-21 multi-week court-approval + refinery-validation rally (+46% cumulative before giving back gains) — the latter is the first time CRML's own event-driven news produced a sustained rally rather than a same-day fade.

postLose.note: Two distinct downside patterns: CRML's own genuinely positive news has twice triggered same-day selling (-5.99% on the binding EuLi agreement, May 18; -6.29% on the Kenya tender advancing, Jul 23), while the Sep 21-28 pullback (-18%) was profit-taking after a run rather than a reaction to bad news — a different, less alarming mechanism worth distinguishing ahead of the Oct 22 EGM.

spotSizing.reason: Moonshot sizing — regulatory_approval catalystType is a lane leader (+5.3pp median excess vs +2.0pp overall, n=8 completed windows), a real tailwind, but real merger-mechanics dilution (EuLi at ~41% of combined co, floating 0.025-0.045 exchange ratio) plus the unresolved cash-gap disclosure status argue against sizing above the 3% floor.

stopPreCatalyst.note: Below Entry 2 zone before the Oct 22 EGM = market pricing in vote failure, an unresolved cash gap, or a fresh dilutive filing. Set wider than the regulatory_approval bucket's own -25% median MAE per the feedback prior.

stopPostCatalyst.note: If the Oct 22 EGM vote fails, the cash-gap issue resurfaces unresolved, or the Kenya tender is lost, exit — a failed dated binary is different from ordinary post-run profit-taking
